full_judgment: 2. The present lave petitioner and pro-forma respondent Nos. 51-54 herein, as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No.71 of 2003 in the Court of learned Assistant Judge, Hajiganj Chandpur for declaration of title and partition claiming separate shaham for .75 acre of land. The material case of the plaintiffs, in short, was that Abbas Ali was the owner of five anna six ganda two kara two kranti share of the land of C.S. Khatian No.71 of Mouza-Motani of Upazila Hajigonj, under District-Chandpur. The said Abbas Ali died before C.S. operation leaving behind two sons and three daughters namely Bande Ali, Akrammudin, Alekjan Bibi, Elemjan Bibi and Sabjan Bibi. That during C.S. operation, Bande Ali and Akramuddin fraudulently did not record the names of their sisters in C.S. record of rights. That Elemjan Bibi became widow with one son and three daughters namely Muslim Uddin, Meherunnessa, Ulfatenessa and Arabennessa and she was then taken by her brother Akramuddin to their paternal home and since then Elemjan Bibi was residing in her paternal home by erecting a dwelling house thereon. That Muslim Uddin died before Elemjan leaving behind only son Anwarullah. Elemjan orally gifted 1.28 acres of land in favour of the son Anwar Ullah and delivered possession of the same. That Arabennessa, the daughter of Elemjan died leaving one son and two daughters namely Aynuddin, Eannatunnesa and Henzil Begum. That daughters of Elemjan namely, Meherannessa and Ulfatunnessa admitted the ownership of Anwar Ullah by mutating a registered "Muktipatra" dated 17.02.1954. That Anwar Ullah transferred 27 decimals of land and the rest 1.01 acres of land has been mutated in his name in Kharize Khatian No.75 and he possessed the same on payment of rent. Those lands have been recorded in the name of Anwar Ullah in B.S. Khatian also. That Anwar Ullah possessed 37 decimals of land from the estern part of Plot No.4 and transferred that in favour of the plaintiffs vide kabala dated 28.05.1995 and also delivered possession of the same in favour of the plaintiffs. That the plaintiffs have been possessing that land by erecting dwelling house therein. That .03 decimals of land of the plaintiffs has been attracted in the care road and rest 34 decimals of land are under possession of the plaintiffs from the eastern side of Plot No.4. That A. Khaleque, A Malek and Mafia Khatun the other co-sharers of the suit holding exchanged their land to the plaintiffs vide exchange deed dated 12.08.1999 and thus the plaintiffs are owner of total 71 decimals of land of Plot No.4 and 4 decimals of land of Plot No. 39. The defendant No.1 intended to purchase 37 decimals of land of Plot No.4 from Anwar Ullah but he did not agree. That the defendant No.1 with the aid and assistance of Bande Ali Mia filed appeal under Section 31 of the Bengal Tenancy Rules against the record of the plaintiffs and also created an antedated Bainapatra and instituted Title Suit No. 41 of 2000 before the Assistant Judge, Hajigonj, Chandrapur and knowing about that suit, the plaintiffs filed application for addition of party in that suit which was ultimately allowed. Against that order the defendant No.1 filed Civil Revision before the High Court Division which was allowed and the order of addition of party was set aside. Later the said Title Suit No.41 of 2000 was dismissed ex-parte. Against that judgment and decree the defendant No.1 preferred appeal being Title Appeal No.157 of 2001 which was ultimately allowed ex-parte. The plaintiffs then instituted Title Suit No.59 of 2000 for permanent injunction which was decreed. The defendant No.1 preferred Title Appeal No.68 of 2004 against that judgment and decree which was dismissed. This plaintiffs thus are possessing their land peacefully. Since there was no partition by metes and bounds and boundary dispute arose among the co-sharers the plaintiffs were constrained to file this suit.
